newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turks to sell Iran/Iraq 135,000 T sugar via trade.
newsitem.headline: Turks to sell Iran/Iraq 135,000 T sugar via trade.

text.p: Turkey's state sugar refinery, Turkseker, is planning to sell about 135,000 tonnes of sugar to be destined to Iran and Iraq by means of local traders at prices of about $15 to $35 per tonne over Paris prices, a senior company official said on Tuesday.
"We are now selling local trading companies some 35,000 tonnes more of sugar in addition to our sales of 50,000 tonnes in January," said the official, who declined to be named.

Turkey sold 50,000 tonnes of sugar to two local companies in January through a tender. But Turkseker officials have said they will not hold tenders for future sales but rather agree with buyers on a price.
"We will also ask the government to sell 100,000 tonnes more to trading companies from our stocks in the same manner," the official told Reuters. "Such sugar is destined to mainly Iran and Iraq."

He said several local trading companies had been buying Turkseker sugar, produced at 25 refineries throughout Turkey, to re-export to neighbouring countries. Asked about the pricing of the sugar sales, he said: "The prices differ depending on the location of the loading refinery."
Turkey has a surplus of 300,000 tonnes of sugar from 1996/97 from output of 1.85 million tonnes and imports from the year before.
